back: All the organisms of one species living in the same area at the same time, able to interbreed.
All the populations of different species living and interacting in the same area at the same time.
A relatively self-contained, interacting community of organisms together with its abiotic environment.
The role of a species in its ecosystem: its food, position, tolerances and interactions with other species.
Habitat is the place (address); niche is the role (job). Two species can share a habitat but not a niche.
Ecosystem and habitat diversity; species diversity (richness and evenness); genetic diversity within species.
Richness: number of species. Evenness: how equally individuals are spread among the species.
Allows adaptation to new diseases or climate; reduces inbreeding depression; supplies alleles for breeding crops and livestock.
Two species cannot occupy exactly the same niche in the same habitat for long: one outcompetes the other.
